text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The 1997 Budget will be a "no-surprises" Budget designed to reduce consumption, increase productivity and encourage savings, while at the same time keeping the nation's books balanced.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday that the decision to allow concerts by foreign entertainers to be staged in the country will depend on the Michael Jackson show at Stadium Merdeka on Sunday and Tuesday. If the crowd misbehaved, the government would not allow another such concert, he said.

- Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd's executive chairman Wan Adli Wan Ibrahim said the company's sewerage services will not be affected by the government's suspension of its billing and collection of charges.

- Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim's sixth budget today is expected to continue to stress on managing the strong growth of the Malaysian economy and price stability, while addressing some recent concerns.
- Limits for loadings in insurance premiums of comprehensive motor policies will be reduced while those for third-party covers will be raised from November 1.
- Companies are not required to carry their reference numbers on all documents and the recent amendments to Section 121 and 338 of the Companies Act 1965 would only be enforced on August 15 1997.

- The government's 1997 Budget to be unveiled by Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim today will focus on three objectives: boosting labour productivity, controlling inflation and cutting the balance of payments current account deficit.
- Most vehicle owners will pay less for their comprehensive motor insurance policies from next month under new Bank Negara guidelines to insurers.
